STEP 1 - Scene: A tuna salad (flaked tuna mixed with diced celery, shredded carrot, and small pieces of what look like red onion or olive bits) in a white square bowl, photographed from above. A plate of shredded carrot sits at the left edge, which is not part of this meal.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square white bowl is about 20 cm across its width. Vessel area ≈ 20 x 20 = 400 cm² (treating it as a square; the rounded corners reduce this slightly, so I use ~370 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: Tuna (flaked, mayonnaise-dressed), celery (diced), carrot (shredded), small dark pieces (likely olive or onion).

STEP 4 - Area: The food pile covers roughly a 9 x 9 cm central area, about 25% of the vessel. Tuna ~15%, celery ~4%, carrot ~3%, other bits ~3%. Total food coverage ~25%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile covers ~0.25 x 370 ≈ 93 cm² with an average height of ~2.5 cm, giving ~230 ml gross volume. Tuna ~15% (≈55 cm²) x 2.5 cm ≈ 140 ml; celery ~4% (≈15 cm²) x 1.5 cm ≈ 22 ml; carrot ~3% (≈11 cm²) x 1 cm ≈ 11 ml; other ~3% ≈ 10 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Tuna salad (mayo-dressed, dense) at 0.9: 140 ml → 126 g. Celery at 0.6: 22 ml → 13 g. Carrot at 0.6: 11 ml → 7 g. Olive/onion bits at 0.8: 10 ml → 8 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Tuna mayo salad ~190 kcal/100 g (mayonnaise-bound tuna). Celery ~16 kcal/100 g. Carrot ~41 kcal/100 g. Olives/onion ~100 kcal/100 g.
- Tuna salad: 126 g × 1.9 = 239 kcal
- Celery: 13 g × 0.16 = 2 kcal
- Carrot: 7 g × 0.41 = 3 kcal
- Olive/onion: 8 g × 1.0 = 8 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 154 g of tuna salad with vegetables, roughly 250 kcal, is plausible for a modest visible portion covering about a quarter of a bowl.
